stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has secured a $190 million Series C funding round aimed at enhancing co-orbital security and space domain awareness. The investment underscores the Department of Defense's increasing focus on advanced technologies to protect national interests in orbit. With a valuation now at $1.6 billion, True Anomaly is positioning itself as a key player in the defense space.
stories.soWhat: This funding is a clear signal that the DoD is serious about co-orbital threats, and True Anomaly is riding the wave of urgency.

stories.head: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant clears design review
stories.body: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant for the Department of Defense has successfully passed its critical design review, paving the way for future development. This vehicle aims to provide flexible cargo and crew transport capabilities, which could be vital for military logistics. The real challenge will be ensuring that it meets the ambitious timelines set by the DoD.
stories.soWhat: If Sierra can deliver on time, it may just set the standard for future military space transport, but that's a big 'if' in this industry.

stories.head: Loft Orbital partners with NASA for AI Earth observation
stories.body: Loft Orbital is collaborating with NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory to test AI models on spacecraft for Earth observation. This partnership aims to enhance the efficiency of data collection and analysis, potentially reducing the need for human oversight. The financial terms of the deal remain undisclosed, but the implications for automated surveillance are substantial.
stories.soWhat: This is yet another example of how AI is being positioned as a substitute for human expertise, which might not be a comforting thought for those in the field.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
